meta.title: Baseline — Brain health over time
meta.description: Short everyday activities that build your personal brain-health baseline and notice meaningful change early.

common.simulatedHint: This data is synthetic, for demonstration only.
common.screeningNotice: Baseline is a screening and monitoring tool. It does not diagnose any condition.

home.tagline: Know your usual. Notice change early.
home.intro: A few minutes of everyday activities, like remembering a shopping list or sorting medicines, build a picture of what is normal for you. Baseline then looks for meaningful change over time.

steps.title: Set your baseline
steps.body: Short activities for one week show what is usual for you.

steps.title: Check in briefly
steps.body: A few minutes a day, plus how you slept and how you feel.

steps.title: Get clear next steps
steps.body: Healthy habits, a repeat check, or a summary for your doctor when it helps.

dashboard.baselineBody: {done} of {total} short sessions done. Up to two a day works best.
dashboard.resetConfirm: This deletes everything stored on this device. Continue?

status.title: What we see so far
status.offline: We could not reach the results service. Your sessions are saved on this device and will be looked at next time.

body.stable: No meaningful change in what we measure. This is not a full health check. If anything worries you, talk to your doctor any time.
body.watch_context: Your activities were a little different recently. {context} often affects how we feel and focus. We'll do a short check again in a few days.
body.watch: Some of your recent results were different from your usual. This happens for many reasons. We'll do a few short checks over the next days to understand it better.
body.review: Over the last few checks, some results have stayed different from your usual. This is not a diagnosis. It is a good reason to talk with a doctor, who can look at the full picture.
body.urgent: What you described needs urgent medical help. Please call 998 now or go to the nearest emergency department.

status.gap: It has been a while since your last session. A short one today keeps your picture up to date.

onboarding.welcomeBody: We will ask a few questions, check that you can hear and see comfortably, and explain how your information is used. It takes about 3 minutes.
onboarding.aboutBody: This helps us compare you fairly. You can skip anything you prefer not to share.
onboarding.familiarityBody: There are no right answers. This helps us give the right amount of guidance.
familiarityQuestions: Do you use a smartphone every day?
Do you send messages or make video calls on your phone?
Do you feel comfortable trying new apps?
onboarding.hearingPrompt: Press Listen. Can you hear the voice clearly?
onboarding.hearingSample: Hello. This is how Baseline will read instructions to you.
onboarding.noVoice: Your device has no voice for this language. Instructions will be shown as text.
onboarding.visionPrompt: Can you read this sentence easily?
onboarding.assistedPrompt: Will someone usually help you with the activities?
onboarding.consentBody: Choose what Baseline may use. You can change these at any time, and delete all your data.

core.title: Activities and check-ins
core.body: Your activity results and daily check-ins, stored on this device.

informant.title: Family member input
informant.body: A person you choose answers short questions about everyday life.

device.title: Health devices
device.body: Readings such as blood pressure, glucose and sleep.

records_import.title: Health record summaries
records_import.body: Summaries you import, such as screening results.

genomics.title: Genetic information
genomics.body: Only shared with your clinician, never shown as a score.

share_clinician.title: Share with my clinic
share_clinician.body: Only when you choose to send a summary.

research_use.title: Help improve Baseline
research_use.body: Anonymous data to check fairness and accuracy.

onboarding.finishBody: Next, short sessions over about a week will set your personal baseline. Each takes about 5 minutes.

checkin.title: Quick check-in
checkin.intro: A few questions about today. This helps us understand your results.
checkin.sleepHours: How many hours did you sleep last night?
checkin.loneliness: How lonely have you felt recently?
checkin.ill: Are you unwell or in pain today?
checkin.newMedication: Have you started or changed a medicine this week?
checkin.caffeine: Have you had coffee or tea in the last hour?
checkin.redFlag: Right now, do you have sudden confusion, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or a sudden severe headache?

urgent.title: Please get help now
urgent.body: What you described needs urgent medical help. Please call 998 now or go to the nearest emergency department. If someone is with you, ask them to help.
urgent.back: I made a mistake, go back

shopping.name: Shopping for a family gathering
shopping.intro: You are buying food for a family gathering. Look at the shopping list and try to remember every item. You will see it for 20 seconds.
shopping.recallTitle: Which items were on your list?
shopping.recallBody: Tap every item that was on the list, then press Done.
shopping.delayedIntro: Earlier you saw a shopping list. Let's see which items you still remember.

quick.name: Coffee time
quick.introSimple: When the coffee cup appears, tap the big button as fast as you can.
quick.introChoice: Now a coffee cup or a teapot can appear. Tap the button that matches it as fast as you can.
quick.tooSoon: Too soon. Wait for the cup.

medication.name: Weekly pill organizer
medication.intro: Your doctor gave you new instructions. Put each medicine in the right times of day: morning, noon or night.

session.doneBodyBaseline: Session saved. {left} more sessions to set your baseline.
session.doneBodyBaselineComplete: Session saved. Your personal baseline is now set.

design.title: Design system
design.intro: Building blocks for Baseline: large text, large touch targets, calm colors, and right-to-left support.

stateHints.stable: No meaningful change in what we measure.
stateHints.watch: Something changed. We will check again soon.
stateHints.review: Worth discussing with a doctor. Not a diagnosis.
